The '''2018–19 New Zealand Football Championship''' season (currently known as the '''ISPS Handa Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the fifteenth season of the NZFC since its establishment in 2004. Ten teams competed in the competition with [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] and [[Team Wellington]] representing the ISPS Handa Premiership in the [[2019 OFC Champions League]] after finishing Champions and Premiers (Auckland City) and runner-up (Team Wellington) respectively in the [[2017–18 New Zealand Football Championship|2017–18]] competition.

Notes:
* The match between Southern United and Auckland City in Round 3 was abandoned at 0–0 after 47 minutes due to the pitch becoming unplayable, it will be rescheduled for 14 February 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hyslop |first1=Liam |title=Hamilton Wanderers continue strong start to national league season |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/domestic/108170466/hamilton-wanderers-continue-strong-start-to-national-league-season |agency=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=28 October 2018}}</ref>
* Waitakere United were tied with Wellington Phoenix Reserves at the end of Round 3 in last place.
* The match between Canterbury United and Tasman United was cancelled due to the [[Christchurch mosque shootings]] and awarded as a 0–0 draw.<ref name="cancelled">{{cite news |title=Canterbury United end regular season ahead of Team Wellington |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/domestic/111337102/canterbury-united-end-regular-season-ahead-of-team-wellington |publisher=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=17 March 2019}}</ref>
